Based on my investigation, the root cause is clear:

- The AWS Java SDK (v1.11.x) sends S3 PUT requests with `X-Amz-Content-Sha256: STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` — the body is sent using "aws-chunked" transfer encoding with chunk-signature extensions (see the `93;chunk-signature=...` lines in the request body).
- In `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py`, `ProxyListenerS3.forward_request` calls `check_content_md5(data, headers)` on the **raw** body as received. Since the body is still chunk-encoded (containing chunk-size headers and `chunk-signature` fields), the computed MD5 over that raw data will never match the `Content-MD5` header (which is the MD5 of the **decoded** payload). Hence the `BadDigest` error.
- This check was added/changed after 0.13.0 (in the `latest` image), which matches the user's report that 0.13.0 works but `latest` fails.
- The fix belongs in `localstack/services/s3/s3_listener.py`: the MD5 integrity check must decode the aws-chunked payload (when `X-Amz-Content-Sha256: STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-PAYLOAD` is present) before computing the digest — e.g., using `parse_chunked_data` from `localstack/utils/http_utils.py` (which already handles chunk extensions). The `CONTENT_SHA256_HEADER` and `STREAMING_HMAC_PAYLOAD` constants are already defined in this file, confirming this is where the streaming-payload handling is expected to live.
